text:
ops-bot: INCIDENT detected for runtime-service: queue_depth=96% | error_rate +12% in 2m | p99 latency 1.8s -> paging #eng-oncall
Samir K: got the page, looking now. first check: is this global or region-specific?
Leah P: I'm seeing traffic spike from us-west-2, lots of long running generate calls (seq len 2048). memory pressure on the serving nodes.
Tanya R: confirming, logs show many requests stuck on KV cache load and a handful of 504s from the frontend.
Connor M: priority: keep P0 customers online. we should consider short-term shedding and tightening timeouts.
Maya S: agree — suggested immediate mitigations: 1) lower max_inflight on runtime pods, 2) disable expensive rerank step, 3) apply org-level emergency rate limits to the top 5 noisy tenants.
Samir K: I'll coordinate the runtime change. which direction for max_inflight? reduce to force shedding or increase to allow throughput?
Tanya R: reduce. long tails are saturating memory and making GC longer. lower concurrency will reduce OOMs and let healthy requests succeed. target: from 256 -> 64 for the busiest nodepools.
Leah P: +1. also reduce request timeout from 30s -> 12s to avoid long-lived slots.
Connor M: I'll flip the rerank feature flag for the cluster to off (heavy CPU).
Maya S: I'll prepare rate-limit rules for nginx: per-org token-bucket 100r/s burst 200 for those five tenants.
Samir K: executing runtime patch now. using control plane API to set MAX_INFLIGHT per pool:```bash
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/runtime/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"pool":"us-west-2-heavy","env":{"MAX_INFLIGHT":"64","REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS":"12000"}}'
```
ops-bot: deploy started: config-update-1855001234 -> rollout canary 10%
Leah P: can someone patch the gateway rate limit? Maya?
Maya S: on it. envoy config snippet for the emergency rule:```yaml
- name: org_emergency_limit
  rate_limit:
    requests_per_unit: 100
    unit: second
    burst: 200
    match:
      - request_header:
          header_name: x-org-id
          exact_match: "ORG-12345"
```
Maya S: pushed to gateway control plane, canaryed to 5% of traffic now.
Tanya R: logs show immediate drop in queue_depth from 96% -> 70% after canary config applied. good signal.
Connor M: rerank feature flag off: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://flags.internal/feature/disable" -d '{"flag":"heavy_rerank","scope":"runtime-cluster"}'
```
Samir K: canary of max_inflight change to 10% is healthy, rolling to 100% now.
ops-bot: rolling update events: pod 12/120 restarted -> 75% ready -> 100%
Leah P: watch p95/p99 — initial data looks promising. p99 down to 600ms from 1.8s in us-west-2.
Maya S: rate-limits on the five noisy orgs are active. one org (ORG-9999) is throttled to 40% of normal. need customer comms?
Connor M: assign severity and impact: impact = degraded for large-batch-generation customers, partial throttling for high-volume orgs, potential transient 429s. severity = SEV3 right now, escalate if errors > 15%
Samir K: list of affected customers pulled from telemetry: ORG-9999, ORG-12345, ORG-22222, ORG-77700. I'll open a consolidated CS ticket with the brief.
Tanya R: adding mitigation notes: - reduced MAX_INFLIGHT to 64 - REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS 12000 - disabled heavy_rerank - applied per-org RB rate limits for top 5 tenants - gateway canary done -> full
Samir K: ops checklist next: 1) Monitor for regressions for 30m 2) If error_rate climbs again, enable progressive shedding by priority (background=reject, foreground=allow) 3) Prepare rollback: restore MAX_INFLIGHT=256 and re-enable rerank
Leah P: I'm taking on-call handoff at 06:00 UTC. Samir, if things stabilize please note any follow-ups for my shift.
Samir K: noted. I'll maintain watch for 20m then handoff summary.
Maya S: customer comms draft: "We're throttling high-volume generation jobs temporarily to protect cluster stability. If you're impacted, contact support; we're reducing backlog and will re-enable full throughput as soon as safe." ping @Customer Success for tailored notes.
Connor M: FYI I'm scheduling a follow-up runbook update — add emergency knobs: max_inflight, request_timeout, per-org rate-limit template, disable-rerank flag.
Tanya R: metrics to watch: runtime.queue_depth, node.mem_free, p95_latency, errors_5m. alert if queue_depth > 85% after mitigation.
ops-bot: INCIDENT update: mitigations applied, metrics improving. status=mitigated (monitoring).
Samir K: handing off to Leah in 20m. current state: stable after full rollout, error_rate down to baseline, p99 improved. followups: refine per-tenant quotas and add a slow-path rejection for low-priority batch jobs in the router.
Leah P: thanks Samir. taking watch. I'll post a summary to #incidents and update the incident timeline and severity if status changes.
Maya S: tagging for postmortem: heavy_rerank should have load-shedding guardrails. consider adaptive timeouts for seq>1024.
Connor M: agreed. also propose a canary for rerank that checks CPU before enabling per pod.
Leah P: closing this thread for now, will reopen on regression. thumbs up all around :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident closed-> monitoring only. note: incident ran 00:07:19 (start 1855001234, resolved 1855001493)
